mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of linear equations will be represented by two straight lines that intersect exactly at the point (2, 1) on the coordinate plane?
mcqs.explanation: Substituting (2,1) into each equation: 3(2)+2(1)=8 and 2-1=1, both are satisfied, so the two lines intersect at (2,1). The other options fail for at least one equation, so they do not intersect at that point.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand solution of a pair as common point
mcqs.question: For the system of equations 3x − 2y = 4 and 6x − 4y = k, which value of k will make the system have exactly one solution?

options.D: No value of k gives a unique solution

mcqs.answer: No value of k gives a unique solution
mcqs.explanation: The second equation is exactly twice the left‑hand side of the first: 6x − 4y = 2(3x − 2y). If k = 8 the two equations are identical (infinitely many solutions). If k ≠ 8 they are parallel distinct lines (no solution). Hence no value of k yields a single intersection point.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of linear equations represents two intersecting lines?
mcqs.explanation: Equations in option B have different slopes (‑1 and 1), so the lines are not parallel and will intersect at a single point. Options A, C and D are either coincident (same line) or multiples of each other, thus they do not give two distinct intersecting lines.

mcqs.question: Which pair of equations represents two distinct parallel lines?
mcqs.explanation: Both equations have the same left‑hand side (slope = ‑1) but different constants, so the lines are parallel and never meet. Options B, C and D have different slopes, leading to intersecting lines.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of equations represents coincident (exactly the same) lines?
mcqs.explanation: Multiplying the first equation by 2 gives the second equation, so both describe the same line (coincident). Options B and D are parallel distinct lines (different constants), while option C gives intersecting lines.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate graph position to number of solutions
mcqs.question: If the graphs of two linear equations are distinct parallel lines, how many solutions does the corresponding system have?
mcqs.explanation: Parallel distinct lines never meet, so there is no ordered pair (x, y) that satisfies both equations simultaneously. Hence the system has no solution.

mcqs.question: A straight line passes through the points (0, 4) and (2, 0). Which of the following equations represents this line?
mcqs.explanation: The slope between the two points is (0‑4)/(2‑0) = –2. Using point‑slope form with (0,4): y‑4 = –2(x‑0) ⇒ y = –2x + 4 ⇒ 2x + y = 4. Option B matches this equation; the others do not satisfy both points.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand solution of a pair as common point
mcqs.question: Two roads are described by the equations 5x + 3y = 20 and 2x – y = 1. What are the coordinates of the point where the roads intersect?
mcqs.explanation: From 2x – y = 1, we get y = 2x – 1. Substituting into 5x + 3y = 20 gives 5x + 3(2x – 1) = 20 ⇒ 5x + 6x – 3 = 20 ⇒ 11x = 23 ⇒ x = 23/11. Then y = 2(23/11) – 1 = 46/11 – 11/11 = 35/11. Hence the intersection point is (23/11, 35/11). The other options do not satisfy both equations.
